cards.title: Utility and maximum expected utility
cards.hook: When outcomes are uncertain, a rational agent maximises EXPECTED utility, not the best case.
cards.visual:
RouteOutcomesExpected utility
A (short, risky)80% U = +10, 20% U = −100.8×10 + 0.2×(−10) = 6
B (long, safe)100% U = +77 ← choose
formula: Σₛ′ P(Result(a) = s′ | a, s) U(s′)
example: Robot on a slippery floor: forward = 80% target, 20% slip sideways → weigh both.
cards.memory: Average, don't dream: expected beats best case.
cards.trap: Choosing Route A because +10 is the best outcome ignores the 20% −10.

cards.hook: An MDP is the formal model of a sequential decision problem under uncertainty.
example: Up from START: 0.8 up, 0.1 left (bumps wall → stays), 0.1 right.
cards.memory: MDP = States, Actions, Transitions, Rewards (+ γ).
cards.trap: MDP = the PROBLEM model; RL = a LEARNING method used when P or R is unknown.

cards.hook: Rewards now are worth more than rewards later.
cards.memory: γ shrinks the future: level k of the search tree is weighted γᵏ.
cards.trap: The first reward gets γ⁰ = 1, not γ.

cards.title: Bellman equation and Q-values
cards.hook: A state's value = best action's expected (reward now + discounted value next).
example: If Q(s,Up) = 7.9 and Q(s,Right) = 6.2 then U(s) = 7.9 and π*(s) = Up.
cards.memory: Bellman = Best action, Expected, Look one step ahead.
cards.trap: Forgetting R inside the brackets, or forgetting to weight by P.

cards.title: Value iteration vs policy iteration
cards.hook: Two ways to solve the Bellman equations.
cards.visual:
Value iterationPolicy iteration
UpdatesU(s) with max over actionsevaluate fixed π (no max), then improve
Equationsnon-linear (max)evaluation is linear
Stopsδ ≤ ε(1−γ)/γpolicy unchanged
Speedmany cheap sweepsoften fewer iterations
example: n states → n Bellman equations, solved recursively in VI.
cards.memory: VI: Values first, policy at the end. PI: Policy first, refine.
cards.trap: Policy EVALUATION has no max (the action is fixed by π).

cards.title: Q-learning
cards.hook: Learn the quality of each action directly, with no model of the world.
formula: Q(s,a) ← Q(s,a) + α[r + γ maxₐ′ Q(s′,a′) − Q(s,a)]
R⁺ if n < Nₑ (be curious) else u (be greedy)
example: Exploratory agent: observe s, choose a (explore/exploit), observe r, s′, update Q, repeat.
cards.memory: Q = Quality; use the MAX of the next state.
cards.trap: Using the average of Q(s′,·) or forgetting γ.

cheat.title: MDP & RL cheat sheet
rows: Q += α(r + γ max Q′ − Q)
traps: MEU uses expected, not best-case utility.
Slips are perpendicular; walls mean stay put.
Q-learning uses max over next actions.
MDP is the model; RL is the learning method.
